item.title: Indian YouTuber Dhruv Rathee alleges abduction ahead of Delhi protests
item.description: Indian YouTube star Dhruv Rathee alleges he was abducted from home and held for nearly 24 hours without a lawyer.

item.title: Maps show how Israel’s ‘Yellow Line’ keeps squeezing Palestinians in Gaza
item.description: A year into a 'ceasefire', Israel restricts access to 65 percent of Gaza and crams 2.1 million people into the rest.

item.title: Delhi braces for more protests against election chief amid crackdown
item.description: Opposition parties joined by student groups are back on the streets, disrupting New Delhi with flash marches.

item.title: What do emergency and governor rule in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa mean?
item.description: Pakistan has taken control of a province governed by Imran Khan’s PTI. Here's what the move means and what happens next.

item.title: Russia introduces drone classes in public schools
item.description: Russian public schools are teaching children to assemble and fly drones as part of changes to the national curriculum.

item.title: Photos: Gaza mothers endure endless lines as famine fears persist
item.description: Hunger grips Gaza, with over 1.4 million people acutely short of food as aid remains insufficient to meet basic needs.

item.title: Steve Smith breaks Test fielding record as Australia dominate South Africa
item.description: Smith moves to 223 career catches, a record for fielders, as Australia bowl out South Africa for 284 in reply to 390.

item.title: India opposition plans New Delhi protest to demand election chief resign
item.description: Thousands of security personnel have been deployed before a protest rally calling for the election chief's removal.

item.title: Alvarez vs M’billi boxing bout to go ahead in Saudi Arabia despite attacks
item.description: Mexican boxer tells Turki Al-Sheikh he 'fears nothing' and will face M'billi in Riyadh on October 31 'no matter what'.

item.title: If Netanyahu goes, does anything really change for Palestinians?
item.description: Analysts say opposition win in polls may bring only marginal change and no fundamental shift on Gaza, West Bank.

item.title: India protest live: Opposition holds ‘March for Democracy’ to Supreme Court
item.description: Main opposition Congress party leads rally to the top court to demand the removal of the chief election commissioner.

item.title: Countries warn against travel to Saudi Arabia following Houthi attacks
item.description: US, Australia, Canada, Japan, South Korea and New Zealand among countries urging citizens to avoid travel to the kingdom.

item.title: Clashes reported in Yemen as Houthis advance towards Taiz
item.description: Heavy clashes have been reported between Houthi fighters and Yemeni- forces near the strategic southern city of Taiz.

item.title: China sanctions Paraguay, Belize ministers over Taiwan ties
item.description: Chinese Foreign Ministry cites national sovereignty and Taiwan separatist activities as reasons behind the measures.

item.title: Netanyahu demands probe into sources for award-winning Gaza film NAZA
item.description: Documentary draws on 24 anonymous Israeli sources accusing military of killing Palestinians in Gaza using AI systems.

item.title: Ethiopian troops enter Adigrat in Tigray, near the Eritrean border
item.description: Ethiopian government forces entered Adigrat in northern Tigray after rebel fighters withdrew.

item.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards the sea
item.description: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said one of the missiles launched from the Pyongyang area flew more than 900km.

item.title: At least 139 dead as migrant boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes
item.description: At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, have died and 84 remain missing after a migrant boat capsized.

item.title: Saudi Arabia says 1 dead, 11 injured in latest attack on Riyadh airport
item.description: Sunday's strike on King Khalid International airport kills a Pakistani national.

item.title: Bridge washed away by torrent of water in Nepal
item.description: Flash floods along Nepal’s Budhi Gandaki River swept away homes and bridges, forcing residents to flee to higher ground.

item.title: UK PM Andy Burnham says it is ‘clear’ Russia interfered in 2016 Brexit vote
item.description: Claim marks the first time a UK prime minister has publicly acknowledged Russia's interference in the vote to leave EU.

item.title: Iran urges Saudi Arabia to pursue diplomacy after Houthis escalate attacks
item.description: Tehran offers to facilitate talks between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis following deadly strikes on the kingdom.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias leaves trail of destruction across the US Gulf Coast
item.description: Crews rally for massive cleanup effort in Florida and Alabama as Isaias leaves hundreds of thousands in the dark.

item.title: Ceuta or Sebta? Why one city has two names and a disputed status
item.description: Felipe VI’s first visit to Ceuta and Melilla as king brings Spain’s territorial dispute with Morocco back into focus.

item.title: Iran war live: Tehran says Yemen escalation benefits ‘only’ Israel
item.description: Iran says 'deeply concerned about developments in the Arabian Peninsula' after another Houthi attack on Riyadh airport.
